mandatoryFindings.title: Reused inherited-baseline JSON is still interpreted without verifying its consumed buffer
mandatoryFindings.facts: helpers wraps capture and table, and wraps old.safe_bytes for the original source observer, but retains the CORE regular function used by boundary_inventory. boundary_inventory calls json.loads(regular(ROOT / plan.baselinePath)); this regular returns file bytes without comparing them to the bound baseline digest. The earlier source observer hashes that helper in a separate read. The later baseline interpretation is not routed through verified_read or a required exact baseline pin.
mandatoryFindings.pairedEvidence: independent-check-results.json: actual extracted helpers plus exact pinned CORE regular/boundary_inventory, explicit in-memory file/census/identity/capture/time boundaries. Unchanged and changed baseline buffers each yield inheritedMatched6 and no changed/absent flags. Actual verified_read rejects the same changed buffer before JSON parsing. Four explicit real OS/file/fcntl/process guard proofs also pass.
mandatoryFindings.impact: The declared same-buffer immutable-JSON fix remains incomplete at a live resource-boundary consumer. Changed baseline bytes can define which six identities are treated as inherited before any guarantee that those are the reviewed six. This is a source/fake-boundary counterexample, not actual evidence tampering or a demonstrated real gate allow.
mandatoryFindings.requiredFix: Bind the baseline path and digest from the verified exact plan, require that binding before interpretation, and route the reused boundary reader through safe fresh returned-buffer verification. Reject an unbound/changed target before json.loads, with no stale cache and no original-core/source/runtime modification. Add faithful valid/changed/unbound-baseline paired cases and reseal a new author packet.
